writing_guide: Every answer comes from the AMR Kansas City 2026 Medical Protocols; each question cites its section in 'source'.
Items awaiting a Medical Director ruling (TXA, glucagon, atropine auto-injector, oral diphenhydramine) are left out until ruled on.
Prompts and statements 12 words or fewer; explanations two sentences or fewer.

drips.name: Hospital Drips
drips.tip: Monitor only what's on the §IV-B list. Anything else: call dispatch before you leave.

hands.name: Monitor, Don't Titrate
hands.tip: Watch the patient and the pump. When in doubt, stop it, keep NS running and call DMO.

procs.name: Procedures & Devices
procs.tip: Chest tubes, IO and deep trach suction are yours. Vents, art lines, central lines and pacing aren't.

meds.name: Your Own Meds
meds.tip: Drug, route and indication all have to be in scope.

questions.context: Nurse: "Just normal saline at 125 mL/hr."
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Only if you turn it off first

questions.explain: Normal saline is on the AEMT list. You may monitor it and adjust the rate per standing orders.

questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes, if you don't change the rate

questions.explain: Vasopressors aren't on the AEMT list. Call dispatch before you leave; this is a Paramedic transport.

questions.context: Heparin running at 18 units/kg/hr for a PE.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list
Yes, if the pump stays locked
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic

questions.explain: Heparin isn't on the AEMT list. You may not depart with it running; call dispatch for a Paramedic crew.

Yes — midazolam is in your formulary
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic

questions.explain: AEMT midazolam is limited to active seizures. A sedation drip is a Paramedic transport.

questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes — it's on your monitoring list
Yes, if the patient is breathing on their own

questions.explain: Propofol isn't on the AEMT list. Call dispatch for a Paramedic crew.

questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes — it causes little breathing depression

questions.explain: Precedex isn't on the AEMT list, however gentle it seems. Call dispatch for a Paramedic crew.

questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list
Yes, if you check glucose every 30 minutes
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic

questions.explain: Insulin isn't on the AEMT list. It's a Paramedic transport; call dispatch before you leave.

questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes — it's on your monitoring list
Yes, if the heart rate is under 110

questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list

Yes, if BP is at the ordered target

questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list
Yes — it's an opioid like fentanyl
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic

questions.context: A unit of packed red cells is hanging.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes — it's on your monitoring list
Yes, if the unit was checked at the bedside

questions.explain: Blood products are Paramedic-managed. Call dispatch for a Paramedic crew.

questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes — it's saline, like NS

questions.explain: Hypertonic saline isn't normal saline and isn't on the AEMT list. Call dispatch for a Paramedic crew.

questions.context: Magnesium sulfate drip for preeclampsia.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list
Yes, if reflexes are checked en route
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic

questions.explain: Magnesium is Paramedic scope and isn't on the AEMT list. Call dispatch for a Paramedic crew.

questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes — it's on your monitoring list
Yes — you give nitro SL already

questions.explain: SL nitro is in your scope, but a nitro drip isn't on the AEMT list. Call dispatch for a Paramedic crew.

questions.context: Esmolol drip for heart rate control.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes, if the rate never changes

questions.explain: Esmolol isn't on the AEMT list. Call dispatch for a Paramedic crew.

questions.context: Dobutamine at 5 mcg/kg/min for heart failure.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list
Yes — it's not a vasopressor
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic

questions.explain: Inotropes like dobutamine aren't on the AEMT list. Call dispatch for a Paramedic crew.

questions.context: Amiodarone running at 0.5 mg/min after a VT episode.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — monitor it, don't change the rate
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes — and titrate it as the nurse asks

questions.explain: Amiodarone is on the AEMT list to monitor. Don't adjust the rate without explicit orders and DMO guidance.

questions.context: Lidocaine running at 2 mg/min.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes — monitor it and watch for toxicity
Yes — raise it if the patient feels fine

questions.explain: Lidocaine is on the AEMT list to monitor. Watch for ringing ears, numb lips and confusion.

questions.context: NS with 20 mEq KCl, running on a pump.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes — gravity is fine if it runs slowly
Yes — and it must stay on a pump

questions.explain: NS with KCl is on the AEMT list. Potassium runs on a pump at all times; free-flow potassium can stop the heart.

questions.context: Vancomycin running in NS; about an hour left.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
No — antibiotics are Paramedic only

questions.explain: NS with an antibiotic like vancomycin is on the AEMT list. Watch for flushing and itching (red man syndrome).

questions.context: Piperacillin-tazobactam (Zosyn) piggyback running.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes — it's on your monitoring list
No — piggybacks are Paramedic only

questions.explain: NS with antibiotics like Zosyn is on the AEMT list. Watch for an infusion reaction the whole ride.

questions.context: D10 running for a low blood sugar.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
No — dextrose drips are Paramedic only
Yes — it's on your monitoring list

questions.explain: Dextrose drips are on the AEMT list. Check the glucose every 30 minutes.

questions.context: Naloxone drip after an opioid overdose.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — it's on your monitoring list
No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
No — naloxone is only a push

questions.explain: A naloxone drip is on the AEMT list. Watch for re-sedation and for withdrawal.

questions.context: Ondansetron (Zofran) infusion running.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — call dispatch for a Paramedic
Yes — it's on your monitoring list
No — Zofran drips are Paramedic only

questions.explain: Ondansetron is on the AEMT list. Watch for QT prolongation in high-risk patients.

questions.context: The nurse's report lists three drips.
questions.prompt: Tap the drip that needs a Paramedic crew.
questions.explain: NS and amiodarone are on the AEMT list; heparin isn't. One drip off the list makes it a Paramedic transport.

questions.context: The nurse's report lists three drips.
questions.prompt: Tap the drip that needs a Paramedic crew.

narrative.text: NS with 20 mEq KCl on a pump
Fentanyl at 25 mcg/hr; alert and talking

questions.explain: KCl in NS and fentanyl in an alert patient are on the AEMT list. Insulin isn't.

questions.context: The nurse's report lists three drips.
questions.prompt: Tap the drip that needs a Paramedic crew.
questions.explain: Vancomycin in NS and D10 are on the AEMT list. Esmolol isn't.

questions.context: The nurse's report lists three drips.
questions.prompt: Tap the drip that needs a Paramedic crew.
questions.explain: Lidocaine and ondansetron are on the AEMT list. Dobutamine isn't.

questions.context: The nurse's report lists three drips.
questions.prompt: Tap the drip that needs a Paramedic crew.
questions.explain: Naloxone and NS are on the AEMT list. Propofol isn't.

questions.prompt: Any drip in a drug class you carry is yours to monitor.
questions.explain: Only drips on the §IV-B list are yours. Hydromorphone is an opioid, but only fentanyl is on the list.

questions.context: At the bedside you find a drip that isn't on the AEMT list.
questions.prompt: You may still leave if the unlisted drip looks stable.
questions.explain: You may not depart with an unauthorized drip running. Call dispatch; the call needs a Paramedic crew.

questions.context: Amiodarone drip running. En route, the rhythm worsens.
questions.prompt: Can you increase it?

options.text: Yes — the note is enough
Never, under any circumstances
Only with explicit orders and DMO guidance

questions.explain: AEMTs don't titrate without explicit sending-physician parameters and DMO guidance. When in doubt, keep the current rate and call DMO.

questions.context: Vancomycin running. The patient becomes flushed, itchy and hypotensive.
questions.prompt: What do you do first?

options.text: Stop it, keep NS running, check ABCs
Slow the rate and keep going
Give diphenhydramine and keep it running
Wait and report it at arrival

questions.explain: For an infusion reaction: stop the infusion, keep the line open with NS, and assess airway, breathing and circulation. Then notify DMO and the receiving facility.

questions.prompt: Monitoring a drip means you may titrate it to effect.
questions.explain: Monitoring means watching the patient and the pump. It doesn't include adjusting the drug.

questions.prompt: The fallback is: stop the drip, keep NS running, call DMO.
questions.explain: That's the protocol's fallback for AEMTs. Stopping in an emergency and keeping access open with NS is in your scope.

questions.context: AEMT crew, two drips running at pickup.
questions.prompt: Who confirms the pre-departure infusion check?

options.text: Nobody; the hospital already did it
You confirm it has been done
Dispatch confirms it by radio
The receiving nurse, at handoff

questions.explain: On AEMT and EMT crews, the crew member confirms the infusion verification was completed before leaving.

questions.prompt: Which is part of pre-departure infusion verification?

options.text: Set the pump to your preferred rate
Take the hospital pump off the patient
Trace the tubing from bag to patient
Flush the central line before moving

questions.explain: Verify drug and concentration, ordered rate vs pump rate, and trace and label each line. Confirm enough volume and a pump-failure plan.

questions.context: NS with KCl running. The pump fails halfway through the ride.
questions.prompt: What do you do?

options.text: Run the KCl by gravity, slowly
Push the rest of the KCl
Count drops and keep it going
Stop the KCl, keep NS running, call DMO

questions.explain: Potassium must always run on a pump; free-flow potassium can cause cardiac arrest. Stop it, keep access with NS and call DMO.

questions.context: NS running. BP drops and your standing orders call for a fluid bolus.
questions.prompt: Can you give the bolus?

options.text: Yes — NS rate is yours per standing orders
No — only a Paramedic can change NS
Only after the receiving nurse agrees

questions.explain: Normal saline is the one drip an AEMT may maintain and adjust per standing orders.

questions.prompt: You may adjust a lidocaine drip if the patient feels tingly.
questions.explain: Don't change the rate. For signs of toxicity, stop the drip, keep NS running and call DMO.

questions.context: Fentanyl drip running. The patient is hard to wake; RR is 8.
questions.prompt: What do you do?

options.text: Stop it, support breathing, give naloxone per protocol
Halve the rate and recheck
Let them sleep and recheck at arrival
Give midazolam to settle them

questions.explain: On a fentanyl drip, naloxone must be at hand. Stop the drip, support breathing, give naloxone per protocol and call DMO.

questions.context: D10 drip running on a 90-minute transfer.
questions.prompt: How often do you check the glucose?

options.text: Every 2 hours
Every 30 minutes
Only at arrival
Only if the patient complains

questions.explain: Check the blood glucose every 30 minutes on a dextrose drip.

questions.prompt: A steady midazolam drip on an intubated patient is AEMT scope.
questions.explain: AEMT midazolam is limited to active seizures. A sedation drip is a Paramedic transport, however steady.

questions.prompt: On an EMT-only crew, normal saline is the only drip monitored.
questions.explain: EMTs monitor the patient and keep NS running. Other drips need an AEMT or Paramedic crew.

questions.prompt: Potassium in NS must run on a pump for the whole ride.
questions.explain: Free-flow or bolus potassium can cause cardiac arrest. Confirm pump programming before you leave and after any line change.

questions.prompt: NS with an antibiotic like vancomycin is on the AEMT list.
questions.explain: Isotonic fluid with antibiotic additives is explicitly AEMT-authorized. Watch for an infusion reaction the whole ride.

questions.context: Patient has a chest tube draining to a collection device.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — chest tubes are Paramedic only
Yes — passive chest tube monitoring is AEMT+
Only with a nurse riding along

questions.explain: Passive chest tube monitoring is AEMT and Paramedic scope. An EMT-only crew can't take this patient.

questions.context: Patient has an arterial line in the radial artery.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: Yes — just watch the waveform
Yes, if the line is capped
No — arterial lines are Paramedic only

questions.explain: Arterial line monitoring is Paramedic only. Call dispatch for a Paramedic crew.

questions.context: Patient is on a ventilator through a trach.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — ventilators are Paramedic only
Yes, if the settings don't change
Yes, if RT sets it up first

questions.explain: Ventilator management is Paramedic only. Call dispatch for a Paramedic crew.

questions.context: Stable LVAD patient going home; the device is running normally.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — LVADs are Paramedic only
Yes — passive LVAD monitoring is all levels
Only with a perfusionist

questions.explain: Passive LVAD monitoring is authorized at every level. Bring the patient's backup equipment and know who to call.

questions.context: The nurse asks you to flush the PICC before you leave.
questions.prompt: Can you do it?

options.text: Yes, with a saline syringe
Yes, if you use sterile technique
No — central line flushes are Paramedic only

questions.explain: Accessing or flushing a central line is Paramedic only. Leave the PICC alone and use peripheral access if you need it.

questions.context: The patient's peripheral IV infiltrates en route.
questions.prompt: Can you start a new IV?

options.text: Yes — peripheral IVs are AEMT scope
No — only a Paramedic restarts lines
Only through the existing site

questions.explain: Peripheral IV access is AEMT and Paramedic scope.

questions.prompt: Can you place an external jugular IV?

options.text: Yes — any peripheral vein is fine
No — EJ access is Paramedic only
Only in cardiac arrest

questions.explain: External jugular access is Paramedic only. Consider IO if access is urgent.

questions.context: Cardiac arrest. No IV, and peripheral attempts fail.
questions.prompt: Can you place an IO?

options.text: No — IO is Paramedic only
Only in a child
Yes — IO access is AEMT scope

questions.explain: IO access is AEMT and Paramedic scope, for unstable or arrest patients when an IV isn't quick.

questions.context: Trach patient with thick secretions blocking the airway.
questions.prompt: Can you suction past the stoma?

options.text: Yes — deep trach suction is AEMT+
No — only surface suctioning
Only with a nurse's order

questions.explain: Deep tracheal and stoma suctioning is AEMT and Paramedic scope. EMTs suction only the surface of the stoma.

questions.context: Patient goes into VF on the monitor.
questions.prompt: Can you manually defibrillate?

options.text: No — use the AED mode only
Yes — manual defibrillation is AEMT scope
Only after a Paramedic arrives

questions.explain: Manual defibrillation is AEMT and Paramedic scope.

questions.context: Symptomatic bradycardia that isn't improving.
questions.prompt: Can you pace?

options.text: Yes — pacing is AEMT scope
Yes, at the lowest current
No — pacing is Paramedic only

questions.explain: Transcutaneous pacing is Paramedic only. Call DMO and consider diverting.

questions.context: Unstable narrow-complex tachycardia en route.
questions.prompt: Can you cardiovert?

options.text: No — cardioversion is Paramedic only
Yes — it's like defibrillation
Yes, if the patient is sedated

questions.explain: Synchronized cardioversion is Paramedic only. Call DMO and consider diverting.

questions.context: You acquire a 12-lead on a chest pain patient.
questions.prompt: Can you interpret it?

options.text: No — acquisition only
Yes — to recognize a STEMI
Yes — for any diagnosis

questions.explain: AMR KC medical direction lets AEMTs read 12-leads to recognize a STEMI. Beyond that, consult a Paramedic or DMO.

questions.context: Receiving hospital wants time-critical labs drawn.
questions.prompt: Can you draw the blood?

options.text: No — phlebotomy is Paramedic only
Only from the existing IV
Yes — phlebotomy is AEMT scope

questions.explain: AEMTs and Paramedics may draw blood samples for time-critical diagnoses per approved procedures.

questions.context: Combative patient who is a danger to the crew.
questions.prompt: Can you give sedation per the behavioral protocol?

options.text: No — behavioral sedation is Paramedic only
Yes — it's a standing order
Yes, at half the dose

questions.explain: Behavioral sedation is Paramedic only. Physical restraint per protocol is in your scope.

questions.context: The nurse asks you to put on a new nitroglycerin patch.
questions.prompt: Can you apply it?

options.text: Yes — you give nitro SL already
No — transdermal patches are Paramedic only
Yes, if BP is over 100

questions.explain: Applying or adjusting a prescription transdermal patch is Paramedic scope at AMR KC.

questions.context: Patient is on CPAP for CHF.
questions.prompt: Can your AEMT crew take this patient?

options.text: No — CPAP is Paramedic only
Only with RT riding along
Yes — CPAP is all levels

questions.explain: CPAP (Flow-Safe II) is authorized at every level.

questions.context: The airway fails and BVM isn't working well.
questions.prompt: Can you place an iGel?

options.text: Yes — an SGA is all levels
No — airways are Paramedic only
Only in cardiac arrest

questions.explain: A supraglottic airway (iGel) is authorized at every level. Intubation is Paramedic only.

questions.context: Signs of a tension pneumothorax en route.
questions.prompt: Can you decompress the chest?

options.text: Yes — it's lifesaving
No — needle decompression is Paramedic only
Yes, if DMO is busy

questions.explain: Needle decompression is Paramedic only. Call DMO and divert for a suspected tension pneumothorax.

questions.prompt: Working with a Paramedic gives you Paramedic authority.
questions.explain: You work within your own credentialed scope. You don't inherit your partner's.

questions.prompt: An EMT-only crew can take a patient with a chest tube.
questions.explain: A chest tube needs at least an AEMT on the crew. Contact the sending facility and DMO before accepting.

questions.prompt: AEMTs may push meds IV but may not start new drips.
questions.explain: IV push is AEMT scope; IV infusion administration is Paramedic only. Monitoring listed hospital drips is a separate authority.

questions.context: Patient begins seizing en route.
questions.prompt: Can you give midazolam?

options.text: No — Paramedic only
Yes, and for agitation too
Yes — for active seizures

questions.explain: AEMT midazolam is authorized for active seizures only. It isn't for agitation or sedation.

questions.context: Agitated patient. The nurse asks for midazolam to calm him.
questions.prompt: Can you give it?

options.text: No — AEMT midazolam is seizures only
Yes — it's in your formulary
Yes, at a lower dose

questions.explain: AEMT midazolam is limited to active seizures. Agitation needs a Paramedic or DMO.

questions.context: Symptomatic bradycardia; the patient has an IV.
questions.prompt: Can you give atropine IV?

options.text: Yes — atropine is AEMT
No — IV atropine is Paramedic scope
Yes, half the usual dose

questions.explain: IV/IO atropine for bradycardia is Paramedic scope. Call DMO.

questions.context: Glucose is 42; patient can't swallow. IV in place.
questions.prompt: Can you give D10?

options.text: No — dextrose is Paramedic only
Only oral glucose
Yes — D10 IV is AEMT scope

questions.explain: D10 IV is in AEMT scope. Recheck the glucose after you give it.

questions.context: Anaphylaxis. You have epinephrine 1:1,000 in a vial.
questions.prompt: Can you draw it up and give it IM?

options.text: Yes — drawn-up IM epi is AEMT
No — auto-injector only
Only into the thigh muscle by a Paramedic

questions.explain: Drawing up and giving IM epinephrine is AEMT and Paramedic scope. EMTs use the auto-injector only.

questions.context: Cardiac arrest with IO access.
questions.prompt: Can you give epinephrine 1:10,000?

options.text: No — IV epi is Paramedic only
Yes — arrest epi IV/IO is AEMT
Only after three shocks

questions.explain: Epinephrine 1:10,000 for cardiac arrest is in AEMT scope.

questions.context: Hypotensive after intubation at the sending hospital.
questions.prompt: Can you give push-dose epinephrine?

options.text: Yes — it's the same drug
Yes, if BP is under 70
No — push-dose pressors are Paramedic only

questions.explain: Push-dose epinephrine is Paramedic scope. An intubated patient is a Paramedic transport anyway.

questions.context: Severe pain from a femur fracture; IV in place.
questions.prompt: Can you give fentanyl?

options.text: Yes — fentanyl IV/IN/IM is AEMT
No — opioids are Paramedic only
Only intranasal

questions.explain: Fentanyl is in AEMT scope by IV/IO, IN or IM. Watch breathing and have naloxone ready.

questions.context: Patient is vomiting; IV in place.
questions.prompt: Can you give ondansetron IV?

options.text: No — only the ODT tablet
Yes — IV ondansetron is AEMT
Only with a nurse's order

questions.explain: IV/IO, IM and IN ondansetron are AEMT scope. EMTs give it by mouth (ODT) only.

questions.context: Opioid overdose with slow breathing; IV in place.
questions.prompt: Can you give naloxone IV?

options.text: No — IN or IM only
Only after BVM fails
Yes — IV naloxone is AEMT

questions.explain: IV/IO naloxone is AEMT scope; EMTs use IN, IM or the auto-injector.

questions.context: Stable SVT at 190.
questions.prompt: Can you give adenosine?

options.text: No — adenosine is Paramedic only
Yes — it's a push
Yes, if vagal maneuvers fail

questions.explain: Adenosine is Paramedic scope. Try vagal maneuvers and call DMO.

questions.context: The nurse suggests ketamine for pain.
questions.prompt: Can you give it?

options.text: Yes — low-dose ketamine is AEMT
No — ketamine is Paramedic only
Yes, intranasal only

questions.explain: Ketamine is Paramedic scope at AMR KC.

questions.context: Hives and itching after an antibiotic; IV in place.
questions.prompt: Can you give diphenhydramine IV?

options.text: No — Paramedic only
Only by mouth
Yes — IV/IM diphenhydramine is AEMT

questions.explain: Diphenhydramine IV or IM is AEMT scope. Stop the antibiotic infusion first.

questions.context: Pregnant patient starts seizing; eclampsia suspected.
questions.prompt: Can you give magnesium?

options.text: No — magnesium is Paramedic only
Yes — it's an electrolyte
Yes, a half dose

questions.explain: Magnesium is Paramedic scope. Treat the active seizure with midazolam per protocol and call DMO.

questions.context: Stable VT with a pulse; IV in place.
questions.prompt: Can you give amiodarone?

options.text: No — Paramedic only
Yes — amiodarone is AEMT
Only in cardiac arrest

questions.explain: Amiodarone for stable VT and arrest is in the AEMT formulary.

questions.prompt: Any drug you can push, you may also start as a drip.
questions.explain: IV push and IV infusion are separate. Starting an infusion is Paramedic only.

questions.prompt: A drug can be AEMT scope by one route but not another.
questions.explain: Atropine and epinephrine are examples. Check the drug, the route and the indication.
